data.title: PBF Energy Announces Pricing of $500 Million of 0% Exchangeable Notes due 2032
data.description:
PBF Energy Announces Pricing of $500 Million of 0% Exchangeable Notes due 2032

PBF Energy Announces Pricing of $500 Million of 0% Exchangeable Notes due 2032

PR Newswire

PARSIPPANY-TROY HILLS, N.J., Sept. 14, 2026

PARSIPPANY-TROY HILLS, N.J., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PBF Energy Inc. (NYSE:PBF) ("PBF Energy") today announced that its indirect subsidiary, PBF Holding Company LLC ("PBF Holding"), priced $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 0% exchangeable notes due 2032 (the "Notes") in a private offering exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The offering is expected to close on September 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The Notes will be co-issued by PBF Finance Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of PBF Holding (together with PBF Holding, the "Issuers"). The Issuers also granted the initial purchasers of the Notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the Notes are first issued, up to an additional $50 million aggregate principal amount of Notes.

The Notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of the Issuers. The Notes will not bear regular interest and the principal amount of the Notes will not accrete. The Notes will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed, on a senior unsecured basis, by certain of PBF Holding's subsidiaries (the "Guarantors") that guarantee PBF Holding's existing senior unsecured notes, and will not be guaranteed by PBF Energy Inc. The Notes will mature on January 15, 2032, unless earlier repurchased, exchanged or redeemed. Noteholders will have the right to exchange their Notes in certain circumstances and during specified periods. Exchanges will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the Notes to be exchanged and, if applicable, cash, Class A common stock, par value $0.001 per share ("Common Stock") of PBF Energy or a combination thereof, at the Issuers' election, in respect of the remainder (if any) of the Issuers' exchange obligations in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes being exchanged.

The Issuers may not redeem the Notes prior to January 20, 2030, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The Notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations), for cash at the Issuers' option at any time, and from time to time, on or after January 20, 2030 and prior to the 31st scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date of the Notes, but only if the last reported sale price per share of Common Stock has been at least 130% of the exchange price of the Notes for a specified period of time and certain other conditions are satisfied. The redemption price will be equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid special interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date. The Issuers may also redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the Notes at any time prior to the 31st scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date, if the principal amount of Notes outstanding at such time is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes initially issued under the indenture (including any additional Notes issued pursuant to the initial purchasers' option) (a "cleanup redemption"). 

If a "fundamental change" (as defined in the indenture for the Notes) occurs, then, subject to limited exceptions, noteholders may require the Issuers to repurchase their Notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid special interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date.

The initial exchange rate is 10.3306 shares of Common Stock per $1,000 principal amount of Notes, which represents an initial exchange price of approximately $96.80 per share of Common Stock. The initial exchange price represents a premium of approximately 37.5% above the last reported sale price per share of Common Stock on the New York Stock Exchange on September 14, 2026, which was $70.40 per share. The exchange rate and exchange price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events.

The holders of the Notes will be entitled to the benefits of a registration rights agreement pursuant to which the Issuers and PBF Energy have agreed to register the resale of the shares of Common Stock, if any, deliverable upon exchange of the Notes under the Securities Act. The registration rights agreement contains significant limitations, and a resale registration statement may not be available at the time investors wish to resell the shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock, if any, deliverable upon exchange of their Notes. 

In connection with the pricing of the Notes, the Issuers and PBF Energy have entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with one or more of the initial purchasers of the Notes or their respective affiliates or certain other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions cover, subject to anti-dilution adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the Notes, the number of shares of Common Stock initially underlying the Notes. The capped call transactions are expected generally to reduce the potential dilution to PBF Energy's Common Stock upon any exchange of Notes and/or offset any cash payments the Issuers are required to make in excess of the principal amount of exchanged Notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap.

The cap price of the capped call transactions will initially be $123.20 per share, which represents a premium of 75.0% over the last reported sale price of PBF Energy's Common Stock of $70.40 per share on September 14, 2026, and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions.

The Issuers have been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to PBF Energy's Common Stock and/or purchase shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock or other securities of PBF Energy in secondary market transactions concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the Notes, including with, or from, as the case may be, certain investors in the Notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of PBF Energy's Common Stock or the Notes at that time. In addition, the Issuers and PBF Energy expect that the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to PBF Energy's Common Stock and/or purchasing or selling PBF Energy's Common Stock or other securities of PBF Energy or the Issuers in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the Notes and prior to the maturity of the Notes (and are likely to do so (x) during any observation period related to an exchange of Notes, following any redemption of Notes by the Issuers or following any repurchase of Notes by the Issuers in connection with any fundamental change and (y) following any repurchase of the Notes by the Issuers other than in connection with any such redemption or any fundamental change if the Issuers elect to unwind a corresponding portion of the capped call transactions in connection with such repurchase). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of PBF Energy's Common Stock or the Notes, which could affect the ability of holders to exchange the Notes, and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to an exchange of Notes, it could affect the number of shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock, if any, and value of the consideration that holders will receive upon exchange of the Notes.

The Issuers estimate that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $485.0 million (or approximately $533.6 million if the initial purchasers fully exercise their option to purchase additional Notes), after deducting the initial purchasers' discounts and commissions and the Issuers' estimated offering expenses. The Issuers intend to use $25.2 million of the net proceeds from the offering to pay the cost of the capped call transactions, and the remainder, together with available cash, to fund the repayment or redemption, as applicable, of all of its outstanding 7.875% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Notes").  If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional Notes, the Issuers expect to use a portion of the proceeds from the sale of the additional Notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties, and for general corporate purposes. Pending such use, the Issuers may repay other debt and/or invest the net proceeds in short-term, interest-bearing deposit accounts. 

The offer and sale of the Notes, the related guarantees and any shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock deliverable upon exchange of the Notes have not been registered under the Securities Act or any other securities laws, and the Notes, such guarantees and any such shares cannot be offered or sold except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and any other applicable securities laws. The Notes and the related guarantees will only be offered and sold to persons who are reasonably believed to be "qualified institutional buyers" (as defined in Rule 144A under the Securities Act). This press release does not constitute a notice of repayment or notice of redemption of the 2030 Notes.

This press release does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, the Notes, the guarantees or any shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock deliverable upon exchange of the Notes, nor will there be any sale of the Notes or the guarantees or any such shares of PBF Energy's Common Stock, in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, sale or solicitation would be unlawful. This press release is being issued pursuant to Rule 135c under the Securities Act.

Forward-Looking Statements

Statements in this press release relating to future plans, results, performance, expectations, achievements and the like are considered "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These forward-looking statements include, without limitation, the statements regarding the closing of the Notes offering and the capped call transactions, the expected use of proceeds, including the proposed redemption or repayment of the 2030 Notes and expectations regarding the actions of the option counterparties and their respective affiliates. These forward-looking statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors, many of which may be beyond PBF Energy's and the Issuers' control, that may cause actual results to differ materially from any future results, performance or achievements expressed or implied by the forward-looking statements. Factors and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ include but are not limited to the risks disclosed in the filings of PBF Energy and PBF Holding with the Securities and Exchange Commission. All forward-looking statements speak only as of the date hereof. Neither PBF Energy nor PBF Holding undertakes an obligation to revise or update any forward-looking statements except as may be required by applicable securities laws.

About PBF Energy Inc.

PBF Energy Inc. (NYSE:PBF) is one of the largest independent refiners in North America, operating, through its subsidiaries, oil refineries and related facilities in California, Delaware, Louisiana, New Jersey and Ohio. Our mission is to operate our facilities in a safe, reliable and environmentally responsible manner, provide employees with a safe and rewarding workplace, become a positive influence in the communities where we do business, and provide superior returns to our investors.

data.title: BOJ Set to Deliver Fastest Hike of Cycle as Pressure Mounts
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa 




  TOKYO--The Bank of Japan is widely expected to deliver another quarter-point interest-rate increase this week, a move that would mark its fastest hike yet in the current cycle. 



  Markets are almost fully pricing in a rate increase at the BOJ's meeting. That will come on the heels of the Federal Reserve's decision, where it could tighten policy for the first time in over three years. 



  Set against a backdrop of surging energy prices, yen volatility, higher bond yields and tacit policy pressure from the U.S., the BOJ's tone and guidance will be scrutinized for hints on whether it will accelerate tightening further or stick to a gradual approach. 



  Here's what to watch: 





  Speeding Up: The BOJ is expected to raise its policy rate to 1.25% from 1% as policymakers grow increasingly worried about inflation overshooting the bank's 2% target. 



  A hike at the two-day meeting ending Friday would come just three months after the central bank's last rate increase in June, marking the shortest interval since it exited negative rates in March 2024. 



  The BOJ has cited the Middle East conflict, yen moves and artificial intelligence-related demand as key inputs for policy steering. 



  Traders have also taken BOJ officials' remarks and comments from U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent as sealing the September outcome. Some even see a slight chance for a bigger-than-usual hike. 





  Inflation Fears: Japan's underlying inflation is tracking near 2%, sowing greater urgency among BOJ policymakers to contain price pressures than when baseline trends were weaker, said people familiar with the bank's thinking. 



  Still, the speed of price growth--including the impact of higher oil costs triggered by Middle East tensions--remains largely in line with the bank's projections, they added. 



  Whether the latest upswing in crude prices alters their longer-term outlook remains to be seen, as Brent's return to triple digits sends government bond yields higher. 





  Yen Dynamics: What the BOJ communicates will likely have a big impact on the yen. 



  The currency has been on a roller-coaster ride, briefly recovering to seven-month highs against the dollar as expectations for a narrowing Japan-U.S. rate differential supercharged slow-building gains in the wake of joint foreign-exchange intervention by Tokyo and Washington. 



  However, lingering weakness in the Japanese currency remains a threat to import prices. BOJ policymakers worry that a soft yen could magnify Japan's energy bill as Middle East hostilities flare again. The yen was hovering around 154.80 on Tuesday. 



  The yen could also lose momentum if the Fed turns more hawkish, erasing the advantage of a slimming rate gap and restoring the appeal of funding carry trades in the Japanese currency, where investors borrow in cheap yen to invest in higher-yielding assets. 



  A global shift toward tightening could keep Japan's rate gap with other economies wide too. Last week, the European Central Bank raised rates, and markets expect more this year. 





  Future Path: According to people familiar with the BOJ's thinking, a benchmark rate of 1.25% would still keep financial conditions accommodative as that level sits only slightly above the lower bound of the bank's estimates for the neutral rate--which is neither restrictive nor stimulatory for the economy. 



  That would imply that Japan's economy can withstand further monetary tightening. Investors have increasingly priced in a faster pace of rate hikes, with the overnight index swaps market showing a 65% chance of an additional rate increase in December. 



  Analysts say a key factor to watch is the vote count: If two of the board members appointed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and considered to be in favor of loose monetary policy vote against a hike, market participants would interpret that as a sign that the government doesn't like tightening. 



  A more unified decision would signal a stronger consensus among the board on how to proceed with monetary normalization.

data.title: Mitsubishi Electric Invests in OptQC Startup Developing Optical Quantum Computer Hardware
data.description:
Mitsubishi Electric Invests in OptQC Startup Developing Optical Quantum Computer Hardware

Leveraging optical quantum technology and market insights for industrial use

Mitsubishi Electric Corporation (TOKYO: 6503) announced today that its ME Innovation Fund has invested in OptQC Corp., a Japanese startup that develops and provides optical quantum computer hardware. This is the fund’s sixteenth investment to date.

Quantum computing is transitioning from research to practical applications, including the rapid acceleration of technological development for industrial use. These applications require hardware equipped with a large number of qubits, and among the various approaches, optical quantum computing offers superior qubit scalability and energy efficiency.

OptQC is a startup originating from the University of Tokyo. It was established based on technologies developed by the university’s Furusawa Laboratory, a world leader in optical quantum computing. The company’s optical quantum computer features proprietary architecture designed to limit increases in system size as the number of qubits grows. Its hardware technology is highly regarded for its suitability for large-scale systems. OptQC has also established a track record of progress toward practical applications, including delivering its first commercial system to a public research institution and hardware modules to private-sector companies.

Through this investment, Mitsubishi Electric expects to gain early insights into the company’s optical quantum computer hardware development technologies, related components, customers and market trends. The company aims to lead the field of quantum computing and create new business opportunities by applying these insights to its quantum technologies, software implementation knowhow and application development in industrial fields.

data.title: China's Home Prices Continued to Fall in August — Update
data.description:
China's home prices continued to decline in August at the same pace as the prior month, remaining a persistent drag on the world's second-largest economy.

Prices in 70 major Chinese cities dropped 0.17% in August compared with a 0.18% decline in July, according to calculations by The Wall Street Journal based on National Bureau of Statistics data released Tuesday. Of the 70 cities, 49 reported month-over-month price declines.

Compared with a year earlier, home prices in these cities fell 3.3% in August, narrowing slightly from a 3.4% drop in July. Among them, 65 cities reported a year-over-year price declines in August.

For the first eight months of the year, home prices fell 3.5% on year.

China's property slump showed no sign of recovery, despite incremental government measures to ease home purchase restrictions, mortgage rules and down payment requirements.

Data released separately showed property investment fell 19.9% year-over-year in the first eight months, deepening from a 19.2% decline in the January-July period.

Home sales fell 13.1% in the January-August period, little changed from the 13.2% decline in the first seven months.

Property developers' new construction starts fell 24.8% in the January-August period, compared with a 24.0% decline in the January-July period.

data.title: Chinese State-Backed Carmakers Announce Deal Amid Industry Consolidation Push
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang 




  State-owned China FAW Group is planning to take a stake in fellow carmaker Guangzhou Automobile Group under an asset-restructuring deal, underscoring Beijing's push to consolidate the auto industry after years of rampant growth. 



  Guangzhou Automobile, or GAC, said it signed a preliminary agreement to acquire part of FAW's equity interest in an unidentified car-manufacturing joint venture. 



  The Guangzhou-based company plans to issue shares and raise additional funds to complete the transaction, which would make FAW its second-largest shareholder. 



  Although GAC didn't name the joint venture, analysts at both Citi and Bernstein said that FAW's venture with Toyota Motor could be a plausible candidate. The Japanese automaker also has a partnership with GAC in China. 



  GAC, Toyota and FAW didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. 



  Citi analysts see the GAC-FAW announcement as the first concrete move in officials' push to consolidate state-owned automakers. 



  Earlier this month, Chinese government agencies unveiled a five-year plan to overhaul the country's auto industry, pushing for reining in capacity expansion, tighter standards for new entrants, and more support for industry consolidation. 



  "The proposed GAC-FAW transaction appears well-aligned with these policy objectives," analysts at Bernstein said, viewing the development as positive for the an that continues to face significant pressure from overcapacity. 



  If it proceeds, the deal could mark the start of a broader wave of restructuring across the sector, Bernstein said. 



  GAC's Hong Kong-listed shares rose about 15% in early trade before paring gains to 5%. Trading in A-shares remained suspended.

data.title: GO Inc., Waymo Plan to Launch Unmanned Taxi Services in Tokyo
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka 




  GO Inc. and Waymo are planning to start commercial unmanned taxi services in Tokyo in 2027. 



  The Japanese ride-hailing app operator said Tuesday that it agreed with Waymo, the autonomous taxi company owned by Google's parent, Alphabet, to work toward providing unmanned taxi services to the general public. 



  GO and Waymo have been conducting on-road validation in Tokyo since 2025 to adapt Waymo's autonomous driving technology to the Japanese capital's complex road environment, the Japanese company said. 



  GO, founded as a subsidiary of major Japanese taxi operator Nihon Kotsu in 1977, listed in Tokyo in June. 



  The company's major shareholders include Japanese internet company DeNA, the mobile unit of NTT and Toyota Motor in addition to Nihon Kotsu.

data.title: A Camera That Fits With You: Fujifilm Introduces instax Pal 2™ Digital Camera
data.description:
A Camera That Fits With You: Fujifilm Introduces instax Pal 2™ Digital Camera

Second iteration in popular instax Pal™ series features new upgrades with a classic analog look and feel

FUJIFILM North America Corporation, Imaging Division, today announced the launch of the next generation of its unique, ultra-portable instax Pal™ digital camera series - instax Pal 2™ digital camera (hereafter Pal 2). Pal 2 brings a host of new features to the Pal lineup, like an optical viewfinder and new filters and shooting modes.

“When we introduced the original Pal in 2024, some consumers weren’t sure what to make of it,” said Bing Liem, division president, Imaging Division, FUJIFILM North America Corporation. “Its uniqueness wasn’t for some, while others felt it was a perfect go-anywhere camera and loved the overall image-making process that makes Pal different from other cameras. When designing Pal 2, we gathered extensive customer feedback on the original Pal. And with its new look, reminiscent of a classic analog camera, complete with an optical viewfinder, and the ability to send/post images digitally or print images via instax™ smartphone printers or any of our Evo hybrid cameras, Pal 2 puts options in the palm of your hand.”

The free, downloadable instax Pal™ app lets the user’s smartphone act as a remote shutter for hands-free photography. The app also lets users store and transfer their photos via Bluetooth®, while the built-in USB Type-C connector on the camera allows users to connect their smartphone directly to transfer photos into the app. Users can also review their image before transferring via Pal 2’s 1.0-inch LCD Screen on the top of the camera.

Users can make their photos personal with any of Pal 2’s five filter themes, each with six unique effects. Options also include the ability to switch between instax™ mini, SQUARE, or WIDE instant film and frameless formats before adding filters, text, and stickers.

Pal 2 includes instax Animation™ shooting mode – a new way to capture 10 frames and turn them into a playful, flipbook-style animation. Switching modes is quick and intuitive, making it easy to move from still images to animations. To print, users can choose their favorite shot and transfer it directly to any compatible, connected instax™ smartphone printer or hybrid instant camera (sold separately).

Main Feature Recap:

  • Palm-sized design, designed for ages 13+
  • Pal 2 does not print photos - users can print images using instax™ Link series smartphone printers, instax mini LiPlay™ or instax mini Evo™ devices (sold separately). Free smartphone download of the app relating to the applicable instax™ device required. instax™ instant film required for image printing (sold separately). Prints photos in instax™ mini, SQUARE or WIDE formats.
  • Authentic Optical Viewfinder
  • 1.0-inch LCD Screen
  • Camera angle adjustment accessory included
  • Five filter themes, each with six unique effects
  • Download of free instax Pal™ app required for use
  • Holds up to 100 photos at a time before required transfer to free, downloadable instax Pal™ app
  • instax Animation™ shooting mode
  • Wireless Bluetooth® 5.1 smartphone connectivity
  • Built-in USB Type-C connector
  • Accepts microSD Card (not included)
  • Includes USB Type-C Cable, Hand Strap, Camera Angle Adjustment Accessory and 1-Year Limited Warranty

Pricing and Availability

instax Pal 2™ digital camera is expected to be available late September 2026 at a Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price of $169.95 USD and $219.99 CAD. Pal 2 will be available in sleek Black or stylish White color options. For more information, please visit https://www.instaxus.com/cameras/instax-pal-2-digital-camera/.

About Fujifilm

FUJIFILM North America Corporation, a marketing subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation, consists of five operating divisions. The Imaging Division provides consumer and commercial photographic products and services, including silver halide consumables; inkjet consumables; digital printing equipment, along with service and support; personalized photo products fulfillment; film; one-time-use cameras; and the popular instax™ line of instant cameras, smartphone printers, instant film, and accessories. The Electronic Imaging Division markets its GFX System and X Series lines of mirrorless digital cameras, lenses, and accessories to provide a variety of content creation solutions for both still and moving imagery. The Optical Devices Division provides optical lenses for the broadcast, cinematography, closed circuit television, videography, and industrial markets, and also markets binoculars and other optical imaging solutions. The Business Innovation Division offers a full lineup of digital print and toner technologies focused on enabling the digital transformation of businesses and print shops with its offerings of multifunction printers, digital inkjet presses, production toner printers, software, and more. The Industrial Products Division delivers new products derived from Fujifilm technologies including data storage tape products, including OEM and FUJIFILM Ultrium LTO cartridges, desalination solutions, microfilters and gas separation membranes.

For more information, please visit https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region, go to https://x.com/fujifilmus to follow Fujifilm on X, or go to https://www.facebook.com/FujifilmAmerica to Like Fujifilm on Facebook.

FUJIFILM Corporation is a subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation. FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation, headquartered in Tokyo, leverages its depth of knowledge and proprietary core technologies to deliver innovative products and services across the globe through the four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging with over 70,000 employees. Guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles,” we address social challenges and create a positive impact on society through our products, services, and business operations. data.title: Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act
data.description:
Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act

Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Sept. 14, 2026

Three Republican senators and a bipartisan group of five U.S. representatives honored by Chairman Ruslan Stefanchuk; For Country Caucus backs the Russia sanctions bill as the House prepares to take up the Senate-passed version.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine, Ruslan Stefanchuk, awarded the Ukrainian Badge of Honour "for our freedom and yours" to eight Members of Congress, including members of the For Country Caucus of bipartisan U.S. military veterans. The delegation traveled to Kyiv alongside the With Honor veterans organization for the Yalta European Strategy (YES) Annual Meeting, at a time of increased Russian attacks on civilians in the city. YES is one of the few international conferences that still convene annually in Ukraine.

The recipients were:

  • Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma
  • Sen. John Curtis of Utah
  • Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina
  • For Country Caucus Founding Co-Chair Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska's 2nd District
  • Former For Country Caucus Vice Chair Rep. Salud Carbajal of California's 24th District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Wesley Bell of Missouri's 1st District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Jim Costa of California's 21st District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Eugene Vindman of Virginia's 7th District

The award was also presented to With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and author of Courage Can Save US, which profiles Rep. Don Bacon and other bipartisan lawmakers who have served in the U.S. military or FBI and have demonstrated the courage to work across party lines on important national security issues, including the defense of Ukrainian freedom. With Honor led its fourth bipartisan delegation to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

In Kyiv, the delegation received briefings from senior Ukrainian officials, including Ukraine's National Security Advisor and Deputy Minister of Defense. Members passed gasoline stations and grocery stores in the capital that had been recently struck by Russian attacks. Part of the delegation also traveled to Kharkiv, where they met with frontline units and medics and saw additional destruction from Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure. As delegations departed Ukraine on Sunday, a Russian drone struck a train two kilometers from the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying officials out of Kyiv had passed through the same crossing. Ukraine's state rail operator said the diplomatic train may have been the intended target. No casualties were reported.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act passed the Senate on Aug. 7, 2026, by a bipartisan vote of 86-11. It is endorsed by With Honor Action and by the For Country Caucus, the bipartisan group of military veterans in the U.S. House that Rep. Bacon co-founded as its Republican co-chair and where Rep. Carbajal served as vice chair.

Separately, Congress appropriated $400 million for fiscal year 2026 for European capacity building, which the Department of Defense notified Congress it would use for Ukraine. The funds purchase weapons, equipment, and services from American manufacturers for Ukraine's armed forces. The Pentagon has not yet put those funds under contract. With Honor Action calls on the Administration to urgently obligate and disburse these funds in advance of the challenging winter Ukraine faces as it fights an enemy attacking civilian infrastructure.

"There is no substitute for standing in Kyiv while the sirens go off and watching people go about their day anyway. That is what resolve looks like. Ukraine is not asking Americans to fight this war. They are asking for the tools to finish it and for the pressure that brings Russia to the table honestly. The Senate did its part on sanctions last month, and I hope the House will finish the job this week," said Senator Thom Tillis, who led the Senate delegation.

"Twenty-five years ago this week, I was in uniform watching my country get hit. Marking that anniversary in Kyiv, in a city under fire from a dictator who treats borders as suggestions, sharpens what is at stake. We don't bow to dictators, and we don't leave a democracy to fight alone. This honor does not belong to the eight of us. It belongs to the American people who chose to arm a democracy under attack, and the way to honor it is to pass this sanctions bill and keep our commitments," said Rep. Don Bacon, who led the House delegation and is a retired U.S. Air Force brigadier general who was recently profiled in Barcott's book Courage Can Save US.

"My family left the Soviet Ukraine as refugees with almost nothing and were welcomed in America. My brothers and I gave back to our great nation by fighting for freedom in the U.S. military. We need to continue to fight for freedom by standing with Ukraine. This was my second trip as a Congressman, but the first trip where Kyiv was being hit while we were standing in it. The Ukrainians face a dire situation, and they were clear about their ask of America. They did not ask for American troops. They asked for pressure. The Senate passed this sanctions package 86 to 11, and every week the House waits is another week Russia sells the oil that pays for the missiles and drones whose damage we saw up close. The House should pass it this week," said Rep. Eugene Vindman, a retired Army colonel who serves on the House Armed Services Committee.

"Twenty-five years after 9/11, I marked the anniversary in a capital under fire alongside three Republican senators and a bipartisan group of five House members who traveled into a country under attack to stand with a democratic ally. We saw gas stations and grocery stores that Russia had struck days before, and met frontline medics in Kharkiv. On the way out, a drone hit the rail line minutes behind the train carrying officials from Kyiv, two kilometers from the Polish border," said Rye Barcott, Co-Founder and CEO of With Honor and a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. "Putin is escalating against civilians and testing NATO's edge. The Pentagon must put the $400 million Congress appropriated this year under contract without delay. That money buys weapons from American manufacturers, and every week of delay pushes delivery further out as Ukraine heads into winter. The Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by a vote of 86 to 11. The House should take up that bill this week and send it to the President's desk."

About With Honor
With Honor fights polarization in Congress by supporting principled veterans across party lines who pledge to serve with integrity, civility, and courage. With Honor Action works alongside the bipartisan For Country Caucus in Congress to pass critical legislation for our nation. Learn more about our work at WithHonor.org.

Contact: press@withhonor.org

PNR Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Pentair plc Securities Fraud Lawsuit

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rosen Law Firm, a global investor rights law firm, reminds purchasers of ordinary shares of Pentair plc (NYSE: PNR) between March 11, 2025 and July 14, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"), of the important October 2, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

So what: If you purchased Pentair securities during the Class Period you may be entitled to compensation without payment of any out of pocket fees or costs through a contingency fee arrangement.

What to do next: To join the Pentair class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/pentair-plc/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action. A class action lawsuit has already been filed. If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you must move the Court no later than October 2, 2026. A lead plaintiff is a representative party acting on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation.

Why Rosen Law: We encourage investors to select qualified counsel with a track record of success in leadership roles. Often, firms issuing notices do not have comparable experience, resources, or any meaningful peer recognition. Many of these firms do not actually handle securities class actions, but are merely middlemen that refer clients or partner with law firms that actually litigate the cases. Be wise in selecting counsel. The Rosen Law Firm represents investors throughout the globe, concentrating its practice in securities class actions and shareholder derivative litigation. Rosen Law Firm has achieved the largest ever securities class action settlement against a Chinese Company. Rosen Law Firm was Ranked No. 1 by ISS Securities Class Action Services for number of securities class action settlements in 2017. The firm has been ranked in the top 4 each year since 2013 and has recovered billions of dollars for investors. In 2019 alone the firm secured over $438 million for investors. In 2020, founding partner Laurence Rosen was named by law360 as a Titan of Plaintiffs' Bar. Many of the firm's attorneys have been recognized by Lawdragon and Super Lawyers.

Details of the case: According to the lawsuit, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and or failed to disclose that: (1) there was significant destocking of inventory in the Pool channel; (2) as a result, Pentair's sales and operating income were adversely affected; and (3) as a result of the foregoing, defendants' positive statements about Pentair's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis. When the true details entered the market, the lawsuit claims that investors suffered damages. 

To join the Pentair class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/pentair-plc/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action.

No Class Has Been Certified. Until a class is certified, you are not represented by counsel unless you retain one. You may select counsel of your choice. You may also remain an absent class member and do nothing at this point. An investor's ability to share in any potential future recovery is not dependent upon serving as lead plaintiff.
